title: Day 696 — UIF Details $5.8M Recovery From García Luna-Linked Weinberg Network, Earmarks Funds for Guerrero Mountain Schools
detail: On August 28, 2026 (Day 696, Friday), UIF chief Omar Reyes Colmenares returned to the mañanera to detail the mechanism behind the recovery President Sheinbaum had previewed the day before: a civil lawsuit yielded $5,805,693 from companies tied to Mauricio Samuel Weinberg López and Jonathan Alexis Weinberg Pinto, identified as front men for former Public Security Secretary Genaro García Luna. Reyes Colmenares said the network — which received roughly 30 government contracts at inflated prices during the Calderón administration — diverted about 528 million pesos and $727.9 million through shell companies between 2008 and 2018, part of a scheme that also produced a $578.5 million final Florida court judgment in Mexico's favor and drew on legal cooperation with Panama, Spain, the U.S. and El Salvador (61 arrest warrants issued, 17 detentions). Sheinbaum said the newly recovered $5.8M would be the first García Luna-linked funds returned to the public purse and specifically earmarked for schools in the Guerrero mountain region: "El objetivo es que este recurso se destine a escuelas en la montaña de Guerrero." She added that UIF-wide, the unit has blocked 24,622 accounts (7,681 linked to organized-crime members), frozen 8.67 billion pesos, and placed 2,395 subjects under financial monitoring during her administration.

media.caption: UIF chief Omar Reyes Colmenares details the $5.8M recovery tied to the García Luna network

title: Day 696 — Zaldívar Clarifies Constitutional Test for Barring Fugitives From Candidacies
detail: On August 28, 2026 (Day 696, Friday), retired Supreme Court justice Arturo Zaldívar appeared at the mañanera to clarify the constitutional criteria — Article 38 — governing when a person under investigation or with an arrest warrant can be barred from running for office, following questions raised after Sheinbaum's August 25 announcement of a dual-nationality candidacy ban tied to fugitive ex-Tamaulipas governor Francisco Javier García Cabeza de Vaca. Zaldívar said merely having an arrest warrant does not by itself suspend a person's political rights; two elements must be shown together — an active arrest warrant and evidence the person is actively evading justice ("que una persona sea prófuga de la justicia") — distinguishing the constitutional text from how the Supreme Court and Electoral Tribunal have applied it in practice. Sheinbaum said the clarification was needed because "una cosa es lo que dice la Constitución y las leyes y otra lo que" the courts have resolved case by case.

media.caption: Retired justice Arturo Zaldívar explains the constitutional test for barring fugitive candidates

title: Day 696 — Sheinbaum Meets Ayotzinapa Families, Pledges Public Report Before Sept 26 Anniversary
detail: On August 28, 2026 (Day 696, Friday), President Sheinbaum met with families of the 43 missing Ayotzinapa normalistas and called the case "una prioridad de Estado," pledging to exhaust remaining investigative lines, accelerate telephone-communication analysis, and press foreign governments — particularly the United States — to complete pending extraditions, including that of a judge implicated in 2014, Ulises Bernabé. She committed to delivering a public report to the families before September 26, the case's 12-year anniversary, covering new arrests and progress across four priority investigative lines. Sheinbaum said the families "se mostraron muy receptivos y acordamos seguir avanzando"; to date only three of the 43 students' remains have been identified.

media.caption: Sheinbaum meets with Ayotzinapa families, pledges a report before the 12-year anniversary

title: Day 696 — Sheinbaum Says Economy 'Doing Well Despite Tariffs,' Cites 51% Drop in Daily Homicides Ahead of Second Report
detail: On August 28, 2026 (Day 696, Friday), four days before her Second Government Report, President Sheinbaum said Mexico's economy is going "muy bien" despite U.S. tariffs having hit automobile exports, pointing to Plan México and the Polos de Desarrollo para el Bienestar investment incentives as buffers, and declared herself "very optimistic" about the economy, security and living standards: "México va mejor, México va bien." On security, the government reported the daily average of homicides has fallen 51% since the start of her administration — from 86.9 per day in September 2024 to 42.5 per day in July 2026. She also proposed restricting cellphone use in classrooms, saying neither students nor teachers should use digital devices during school hours, citing psychomotor-skill development and pointing to other countries reverting to pencil-and-paper methods.

media.caption: Sheinbaum says Mexico's economy is doing well ahead of her Second Government Report
